title: Expand the Provisioning Plan
subtitle: Turn the role profile into owned, dated tasks
scenario: It is SD-4. You have the onboarding record, the role profile, and the SLA policy. Expand them into the concrete plan the four branches run: one row per task, each with an owner and a due date computed from the start date. This is the plan the whole parallel phase executes against.
input:
Onboarding record: Jordan Lee (H-4021), Logistics Coordinator, start date SD.
Role profile tasks: accounts, hardware, access, payroll.
Owners: accounts -> IT Provisioner; hardware -> IT Provisioner; access -> Facilities Coordinator; payroll -> Payroll Specialist.
SLA policy (business days before start): accounts SD-2, hardware SD-1, access SD-1, payroll SD-3.
Build one row per task with taskId, owner, and due (as SD-N).
instructions: Create one row per task: accounts, hardware, access, payroll.
Set each row's owner from the owners list.
Set each row's due from the SLA policy, written as SD-N (for example SD-2).
Return a JSON array of the four task rows, then validate.
copilotPrompt: Build a JSON array of four provisioning tasks (accounts, hardware, access, payroll). Each row has taskId, owner, and due. Set owner from the owners list and due from the SLA policy as SD-N.
successMessage: Provisioning plan built. Four owned, dated tasks are ready to run in parallel.
editorHelper: One row per task - each with an owner and a due date.

intro.heading: Before the branches run: the plan

sections.title: Expansion turns a role into work
sections.body: The role profile says what the hire gets; the plan turns each entitlement into an accountable task. Expansion is the step where 'Logistics Coordinator' becomes four concrete, ownable jobs.

sections.title: Every task has one owner
sections.body: A task with no owner is how a start date slips. Each row names exactly one accountable owner, so nothing is 'someone will handle it'.

sections.title: Due dates come from the SLA policy
sections.body: You do not invent deadlines here - you apply the governed SLA policy, writing each due date as SD-N. The plan is where policy becomes a schedule.

sections.title: One plan, four parallel branches
sections.body: These four rows unlock together and run at the same time. The plan is the shared contract the accounts, hardware, access, and payroll branches all execute against.

fieldGuide.meaning: The provisioning task this row plans.
fieldGuide.hint: One of accounts, hardware, access, payroll.

fieldGuide.meaning: The single accountable owner of the task.
fieldGuide.hint: Copy the owner from the owners list exactly.

fieldGuide.meaning: The deadline as business days before start (SD-N).
fieldGuide.hint: Apply the SLA policy: accounts SD-2, hardware SD-1, access SD-1, payroll SD-3.

realWorld.soloRebuildPath: You'd expand your onboarding checklist into one row per task with an owner and a due date, then assign them all at once.

bestFit.how: expand the role profile into dated tasks; the plan is data, so a changed role re-expands cleanly
an Item Lists node fanning the entitlements into one task item per branch

takeaway.heading: Provisioning plan built
points: You expanded the role profile into four owned, dated tasks.
Each task has exactly one accountable owner, so nothing is unassigned.
Due dates apply the SLA policy (SD-N), not invented deadlines.
The four rows are the shared contract the parallel branches execute against.
The workflow can now run four provisioning tasks in parallel against one plan.
